title: Online action reducers capture a stale session snapshot across an await and overwrite the whole store with .set(), silently discarding concurrent mutations
description: addExercise() captures `const session = get(state.currentSession)` at line 106, performs network awaits, and at line 211 rebuilds the whole store with `state.currentSession.set({ ...session, exercises: [...session.exercises, newExercise] })` using that stale pre-await snapshot. The same stale-snapshot-then-.set pattern appears in addSet online (sets.ts:163 -> sets.ts:204), markExerciseDone online (sets.ts:98 -> sets.ts:135), and removeExercise online (core.ts:245 -> core.ts:271). replaceExerciseSets (sets.ts:73) does it correctly with .update(); these reducers do not. Any mutation applied to currentSession between the snapshot and the .set is overwritten and lost. addExercise is concretely reachable: its FIRST await, loadLastTimeForExercise() at line 118, runs BEFORE state.loading.set(true) at line 179, so the UI (SessionExercise disabled={$loading} in routes/+page.svelte:225) is NOT disabled during that network round-trip and the user can freely edit existing exercises.
attackOrTrigger: Online. User types a brand-new exercise name (not in recentSessions cache, not yet in lastTimeByExercise) and taps add. addExercise awaits loadLastTimeForExercise() over the network while loading is still false and nothing is disabled. During that window the user edits an existing exercise's notes / a setting / tracking (settings.ts synchronously .set the store) or logs a set. When createExercise resolves, core.ts:211 does .set({...stale session}) and wipes that edit from currentSession. For debounce-synced fields (notes/settings/tracking) the loss is permanent: the 650ms debounced backend push syncExercise() (settings.ts:45-66) reads get(state.currentSession) at fire time (settings.ts:47), which is now the clobbered snapshot, so it persists the OLD value to the backend.
why: A logged set or an exercise-notes/settings edit silently vanishes from the live in-progress session; for debounce-synced fields it is written back to the backend as the old value, so the user's data is permanently lost, not just visually. The user sees their edit disappear mid-workout and is likely to re-enter it, which then races/duplicates.
fixSketch: In every online reducer, do not build the next session from the pre-await snapshot. After the await, use state.currentSession.update((current) => ...) and merge into `current`, exactly as replaceExerciseSets already does at sets.ts:73-81. Also gate input (loading.set(true)) before the first network await in addExercise so the pre-load fetch does not run with the UI live.

verdicts.title: Online action reducers capture a stale session snapshot across an await and overwrite the whole store with .set(), silently discarding concurrent mutations
verdicts.reason: Code-truth check confirms the mechanism exactly as claimed. addExercise() captures `const session = get(state.currentSession)` at line 106 before any await. The first await, loadLastTimeForExercise() at line 118, occurs inside the try block (lines 113-119) strictly before `state.loading.set(true)` at line 179 — so there is a real network round-trip window where loading is false and nothing in the UI is disabled. A second await (createExercise, line 180) follows, also using the same stale `session` closure variable. At line 211, `state.currentSession.set({ ...session, exercises: [...session.exercises, newExercise] })` rebuilds the entire store from that pre-await snapshot with no merge/update against whatever the store holds at that moment — any concurrent synchronous .set() to state.currentSession made during either await window (e.g. from a notes/settings mutation elsewhere) is structurally overwritten and lost, since JS/Svelte store .set() has no knowledge of intervening writes. No guard, version check, or .update()-style merge exists anywhere in this function to prevent it. The mechanism is real and reachable in the source as written.

verdicts.title: Online action reducers capture a stale session snapshot across an await and overwrite the whole store with .set(), silently discarding concurrent mutations
verdicts.reason: Read through core.ts confirms the precise mechanics cited: addExercise() snapshots `session = get(state.currentSession)` at line 106, and when the exercise name is new (not cached in recentSessions/lastTimeByExercise), it awaits the network call loadLastTimeForExercise() at line 118 -- which happens strictly before `state.loading.set(true)` at line 179. There is no intervening guard that sets loading (or otherwise disables the UI) during this specific await window, so the reachability precondition the finding relies on (an unguarded network round-trip during which the rest of the UI is still interactive) genuinely exists in this code, not just in the abstract. The subsequent online-path rebuild at line 211 (`state.currentSession.set({...session, exercises: [...]})`) does use the pre-await `session` object captured at line 106, so any concurrent synchronous mutation to the store made during the loadLastTimeForExercise await (or during the createExercise await that follows) would indeed be overwritten by this stale-snapshot .set(). Nothing in this file forecloses the trigger sequence (type a brand-new exercise name, tap add, then interact with another part of the session while the network call is in flight) -- it's a normal, reachable user action sequence, not a contrived race. My lens (reachability) does not surface a reason to refute; verifying the other files (sets.ts, settings.ts) for the debounce-sync claim and the exact loss mechanism is outside the single file I was scoped to, but nothing here contradicts the finding.

verdicts.title: Online action reducers capture a stale session snapshot across an await and overwrite the whole store with .set(), silently discarding concurrent mutations
verdicts.reason: Confirmed in core.ts: addExercise() captures `const session = get(state.currentSession)` at line 106, then awaits loadLastTimeForExercise() at line 118 — which runs before `state.loading.set(true)` at line 179, so there is a genuine unguarded network-await window where the UI is not disabled. At line 211, the reducer does `state.currentSession.set({ ...session, exercises: [...] })` using the pre-await `session` variable rather than re-reading current state or using `.update()`. There is no sanitizer, try-catch recovery, debounce-flush, or idempotency mechanism in this file that re-syncs or merges concurrent mutations before the final .set — the stale snapshot is written unconditionally. removeExercise() at lines 244-274 has the identical pattern (snapshot at 245, await cancelExercise at 270, blind .set at 271-274). No mitigation is visible in the cited file, so from the already-mitigated lens this finding holds up as a real, reachable defect.

title: Network failure during the final endWorkout of submitEndSession drops the entered mood/notes and leaves the workout un-ended forever on the next sync
description: In submitEndSession online path, exercises are ended via Promise.all (session.ts:309) then endWorkout is awaited (session.ts:330). If connectivity drops during endWorkout, the catch at session.ts:345-352 calls persistInProgressSession(state), which saves the offline record with status 'in_progress' and NO end_mood / end_notes / endedAt (offline.ts:97-108). Contrast the offline branch (session.ts:291-301) which saves status 'pending_sync' WITH end_mood and endedAt. On reconnect, syncOne only calls endWorkout when `record.status === 'pending_sync' && record.end_mood && record.session.endedAt` (offline.ts:269); for a positive-id in_progress record it replays exercises then deletes the record at offline.ts:283-285 without ending the workout.
attackOrTrigger: Online, user opens the end-session modal, picks a mood/notes, taps End. endExercise calls succeed, then endWorkout fails with a network error. App flips offline and persists an in_progress record with no mood. On reconnect syncOne finishes the exercises and deletes the record without calling endWorkout. The workout stays active on the server and the entered mood/notes are gone.
why: The user believes they finished and rated their workout, but the session is never actually ended on the backend and their end-of-session mood/notes are silently discarded. They must notice the session is still 'in progress' and end it again.
fixSketch: In the submitEndSession network-failure catch, persist an end record analogous to the offline branch: status 'pending_sync' with end_mood, end_notes and session.endedAt set, so syncOne's endWorkout branch (offline.ts:269) fires on reconnect.

verdicts.title: Network failure during the final endWorkout of submitEndSession drops the entered mood/notes and leaves the workout un-ended forever on the next sync
verdicts.reason: Code-truth check confirms the described control flow in session.ts. The online path awaits Promise.all(endExercise...) at line 309 then awaits endWorkout at line 330; state.currentSession is only cleared/nulled and the offline record deleted (line 337-338) AFTER endWorkout succeeds. The catch block (345-352) is shared by both awaits: on isNetworkFailure it calls setOffline + persistInProgressSession(state) + hydrateOfflineState(state), passing no mood/notes/endedAt into the persisted call — mood/notes were read into local variables (`mood`, `get(state.endNotes)`) only for the success-path endWorkout call (line 330-334), never attached to the object handed to persistInProgressSession in the failure branch. This contrasts with the offline branch (277-306), which explicitly builds `ended` with `endedAt, mood` and calls saveOfflineSession with `end_mood`/`end_notes` fields. So within session.ts alone, the asymmetry the finding describes — mood/notes captured for the success path but silently absent from the failure-path persistence call — is real and visible in the cited lines.

title: Turning off split-weight with unequal left/right silently rewrites the logged weight to max(left,right), changing the recorded set and volume
description: toggleExerciseSplitWeight(enabled=false) collapses each set's two side weights into a single weight using Math.max(left, right) at weightModes.ts:138, then persists via replaceSets. With per-side weight still on (perSideWeight true, splitWeight now false), calculateExerciseVolumeKg treats the single weight as per-side and doubles it (metrics.ts:20-21: reps * weight * 2). A set logged as left=40/right=60 (volume reps*100) becomes weight=60 (volume reps*120). The lighter side is discarded, total volume inflated, and the change pushed to the backend.
attackOrTrigger: During a live workout the user logs a dumbbell exercise with different left/right loads while split-weight is on, then toggles split-weight off. Every asymmetric set is rewritten to the heavier side and exercise volume jumps.
why: The user's actually-lifted weights are silently altered and session volume mis-computed; the corrupted values are persisted to the backend.
fixSketch: Preserve volume when collapsing sides, e.g. weight = (left + right) / 2 rather than Math.max, or confirm before replacing both sides with a single value.
